learn.hook: A thief steals from the only person who ever trusted him, then something stops him at the railway station.
points: 'The Thief's Story' by Ruskin Bond is narrated by Hari Singh, a young thief who befriends Anil, a writer.
Anil gives him work and teaches him to read and write. Hari steals Anil's money but returns, realising that learning and Anil's trust are worth far more.
Anil quietly knows but says nothing; his trust helps Hari reform (change for the better).
Stories use narrative tenses: simple past for main events (he crept), past continuous for background actions (Anil was sleeping), past perfect for earlier events (he had decided).
'While' usually takes past continuous; 'when' often introduces a simple past action that interrupts.

example.q: Passage: While Anil was sleeping, Hari crept to the mattress. He had already decided to run away. But at the station, as the train was leaving, he remembered Anil's kindness and turned back. Name the tense of each underlined idea: 'was sleeping', 'had decided', 'turned back'.
steps: 'was sleeping' is background going on at the time: past continuous.
'had decided' happened before he crept: past perfect.
'turned back' is a main event: simple past.
example.answer: was sleeping = past continuous; had decided = past perfect; turned back = simple past.

learn.reallife: When you tell a friend what happened at a cricket match, you naturally mix these tenses: 'We were batting when it started to rain.'

games.title: Hari's night
games.prompt: Put the passage events in order
items: Hari crept to the mattress while Anil slept.
He remembered Anil's kindness and turned back.

items.text: While Anil ___, Hari crept to the mattress.
Before he crept to the mattress, he ___ already decided to run away.
As the train ___, he turned back.
We were having dinner when the lights ___ out.
By the time we reached, the film ___.

quiz.explain: The thief, Hari Singh, tells the story in the first person.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the writer character must be the narrator
Mixes up the authors of Footprints without Feet

options: To become a writer of plays
quiz.explain: Anil teaches Hari to read and write, which changes Hari's life.
quiz.mistake: Picks a skill not in the story

quiz.q: Why does Hari return the money?
options: He misses the train and has nowhere to go
He wants to steal more later
He realises that learning and Anil's trust are worth more than money
quiz.explain: He sees that education could make him a respected man, and he values Anil's trust.
quiz.mistake: Gives a practical reason instead of the change of heart

quiz.q: Passage: While Anil was sleeping, Hari crept to the mattress. He had already decided to run away. But at the station, as the train was leaving, he remembered Anil's kindness and turned back. Choose the tense of 'was sleeping'.
quiz.explain: was/were + -ing = past continuous, for background action.
quiz.mistake: Confuses past continuous with present continuous

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: 'By the time Hari reached the station, the train ___.'
quiz.explain: The train left before he reached, so past perfect is used for the earlier action.
quiz.mistake: Uses present perfect in a past narrative

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: 'We ___ cricket when it started to rain.'
quiz.explain: The longer background action takes past continuous; the interruption takes simple past.
quiz.mistake: Uses simple past for both actions

quiz.q: Passage: While Anil was sleeping, Hari crept to the mattress. He had already decided to run away. But at the station, as the train was leaving, he remembered Anil's kindness and turned back. What made Hari turn back?
options: Anil woke up and called him
quiz.explain: The last line says he remembered Anil's kindness and turned back.
quiz.mistake: Invents a reason not in the passage

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to tell a story! Why do I say 'I was flying when I saw a worm', not 'I flew when I saw a worm'?
teach.praise: Swoop-chirp! 'Was flying' is the background, 'saw' is the event. My stories sound so real now!
teach.nudge: Which tense shows something that was going on, and which shows the event that happened?

topics.title: Writing a character sketch: words for change

learn.hook: A thief who becomes a student. What changed inside him, and how do we describe it?
points: A character sketch describes a person's traits, each supported by evidence from the story.
Structure: introduction (who the person is), 2-3 traits with examples, any change in the character, and a closing line.
Hari changes from a thief who cheats to a young man who values education and trust; Anil is kind and trusting.
Words for inner change: conscience (inner sense of right and wrong), remorse (deep regret), reform (change for the better), gratitude (thankfulness).
Word families: trust (noun/verb), trusting, trustworthy, distrust.

example.q: Write one trait of Anil with evidence.
steps: Find what he does: he knows Hari took the money, yet says nothing and keeps teaching him.
Join trait + evidence in one sentence.
example.answer: Anil is trusting: even after Hari takes his money, he says nothing and carries on teaching him.

learn.reallife: Teachers, coaches and employers write similar sketches in reports and references: 'Riya is responsible: she never misses a deadline.'

games.title: Words of change
pairs: inner sense of right and wrong

quiz.q: Which trait best describes Anil in 'The Thief's Story'?
quiz.explain: He gives a stranger work and keeps trusting him.
quiz.mistake: Judges Anil by the theft rather than by his actions

quiz.q: How does Hari change in 'The Thief's Story'?
options: From a student to a thief
From a thief to someone who values education and trust
From a writer to a cook
He does not change at all
quiz.explain: He returns the money, choosing learning and trust over theft.
quiz.mistake: Misses the change at the end

quiz.explain: Remorse is the guilty sorrow felt after doing something wrong.
To reform is to improve one's behaviour.
quiz.mistake: Splits the word into re + form literally

options: An inner sense of right and wrong
quiz.explain: Conscience is the inner voice that tells right from wrong.

quiz.q: What should a character sketch include?
options: Only the character's name and age
Traits supported by evidence from the story
Only the reader's opinion with no examples
quiz.explain: Each trait needs an example from the story to support it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a sketch is a plot summary

quiz.q: Which sentence gives a trait WITH evidence?
options: Meera is generous: she shared her lunch with a new classmate on her first day.
quiz.explain: It names a trait and backs it with an action.
quiz.mistake: Thinks naming a trait is enough

quiz.explain: 'Distrust' means lack of trust; 'entrust' means to hand over responsibility.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have to write about a character who changes. What do I put in a character sketch?
teach.praise: Chirp-chirp! Traits with evidence, and how the character changes. My sketch will be super!
teach.nudge: What do you need besides naming a trait? And what happens to the character by the end?
